chapter: Harlem scene and race in music
title: Pay scales downtown and in Harlem
summary: Downtown paid better, with AFM classes of scale ranking Roseland above Harlem clubs.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Uh huh. Now maybe this is as good a place as any to talk about questions of race.
And discrimination and the role of the black musician. Now you played places ... I don't mean, you personally, but the musician would play downtown and uptown -- uptown meaning Harlem.
Were the conditions different in the two places? Pay better downtown or anything, or was it all the same?

I guess downtown would pay better. The situation there was that, oh, I'm trying to remember ... yes, the downtown pay, I believe was better. It's even hard for me to remember what kind of money we ... as long as -- what I want to say is -- according to the AFM -- the American

Federation of Musicians -- scale, they would have a higher scale downtown, you know, like maybe a place like the Roseland would be a Class A and someplace else would be a Class B, and maybe the Harlem clubs would be a Class B and a Class C, you know. I don't know if there were any Harlem clubs that they considered Class A.
I kind of doubt it. But if they did, they would probably be places like the Cotton Club where or the Ellington or the Calloway orchestra usually played.
